title: How a computer might think
summary: Inspired by Nuel Belnap's "How a computer should think," which gave rise to the four-valued logic FDE, we contemplate, in this article, how a computer might think if we add a fifth value for unknowable or cannot be known. We devise two new five-valued logics, UKN1 and UKN2, called the logics of the unknowable. These are different from the five-valued logic FDEe of the FDE-family. The main difference is in the number of designated truth values. While FDEe takes two designated values, UKN1 and UKN2 have three. The four-valued reducts of these logics are also different from FDE.
